sourceEvidence.claim: Reassortment definition (segmented genomes; influenza; the 2009 H1N1 human-swine-avian pandemic; antigenic shift)
sourceEvidence.quote:
When viruses with segmented genomes (eg,
influenza virus) exchange genetic material.
For example, the 2009 novel H1N1 influenza
A pandemic emerged via complex viral
reassortment of genes from human, swine, and
avian viruses. Has potential to cause antigenic
shift. Reassortment of genome segments.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Complementation definition (nonfunctional protein rescued; HDV requires replicating HBV to supply HBsAg)
sourceEvidence.quote:
When 1 of 2 viruses that infect the cell has
a mutation that results in a nonfunctional
protein, the nonmutated virus “complements”
the mutated one by making a functional
protein that serves both viruses. For example,
hepatitis D virus requires the presence of
replicating hepatitis B virus to supply HBsAg,
the envelope protein for HDV.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Phenotypic mixing definition (pseudovirion; the type B coat determines tropism; progeny 2 reverts to the type A coat)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Occurs with simultaneous infection of a
cell with 2 viruses. For progeny 1, genome
of virus A can be partially or completely
coated (forming pseudovirion) with the
surface proteins of virus B. Type B protein
coat determines the tropism (infectivity) of
the hybrid virus. Progeny from subsequent
infection of a cell by progeny 1 will have
a type A coat that is encoded by its type A
genetic material.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The naked-genome infectivity paragraph (most dsDNA except poxviruses/HBV + ⊕ ssRNA infectious; ⊝ ssRNA + dsRNA not; virions carry RdRp)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Naked nucleic acids of most dsDNA viruses (except poxviruses and HBV) and ⊕ strand ssRNA
viruses are infectious. Naked nucleic acids of ⊝ strand ssRNA and dsRNA viruses are not
infectious because they lack the required polymerases to replicate. Virions of ⊝ strand ssRNA
viruses carry RNA-dependent RNA polymerases to transcribe ⊝ strand to ⊕.

notes: Census: pdfimages lists 0 rasters on both p181 and p182 — PURE VECTOR, the first M-topic with no copyrighted photos. The banner typo MICROCIOLOGY prints twice on 159 (page header + section header) and once on 160; the VLM census auto-normalized it to MICROBIOLOGY (documented VLM-normalization case — the text layer is authoritative). The structure figure's labels interleave in two-column order; the genetics row labels group before the definitions; 'Base Spikes'/'plate' share lines 49-50; the p182 'Viral envelopes' row label emits after its own row content (line 50); the retro-toga-party mnemonic block emits after the indd footer (52 → 54-57). FA's printed mnemonics (Part of a virus; Repeato-virus; the retro-toga-party sentence; Always bring polymerase or fail replication; BOAR; helpful protection) are quoted in the table block for verification only — KYP's own keys are in the mnemonics block.
